Maria: Quick Q — how are we supposed to resolve feature flag scope precedence today? I need something authoritative before we flip the encoder rollout. Specifically: org / project / route / model — which wins? Also how do percent canaries interact across scopes?

Kevin: I thought the rule was 'most specific wins' (model > route > project > org). But I remember a convo where project could override route for safety? :thinking:

Sophi: Confirming: evaluator uses specificity order — highest specificity first. In practice: model -> route -> project -> org -> global default. The first scope that defines the flag value wins.

Sophi: Snippet of the evaluator order we use:```
# evaluation order (high -> low specificity)
1) model:<model_id>
2) route:<route_id>
3) project:<project_id>
4) org:<org_id>
5) global default
```

Sophi: Example: org sets `allow-experimental-encoder: false`, project sets it to `true`, route/model don't define it -> final = true (project overrides org).

Samir: 👍 ok that clears the boolean case. What about percentage canaries though? If project has 10% and route has 20%, do we combine or choose one? We need deterministic behavior for user id hashing.

Sophi: Good call — percent rollouts are resolved by the most specific scope that defines a percentage. i.e., if route defines `rollout_pct`, use route's pct; else if project defines it, use project, etc. We do NOT union percentages. That avoids double-counting and non-determinism.

Sophi: Example: project.rollout_pct = 10, route.rollout_pct = 20 -> evaluator uses 20% for requests matching that route. If route has no pct but model sets pct -> use model pct.

Kevin: Edge-case: what if a higher specificity scope sets `disabled: true` but a lower specificity scope sets `enabled: true`? E.g., model disables, project enables. Model should win and disable.

Taylor: +1. We should also add a guardrail: any model-level `disabled: true` requires a required-review tag/comment and an automatic alert to oncall. Prevents accidental mass disable. I'll open a tiny policy PR and add a test in the feature flags e2e.

Maria: Can someone add this to the eng-platform runbook/wiki? Also include fallback to `global default` when no scope defines the flag. We should list examples for boolean, percent, and audience-based (user list) rollouts.

Samir: I'll add a short doc and example configs. Planning to include these cases:
- boolean flags (first-defined wins)
- percentage rollouts (most-specific-defined wins, deterministic hashing by user_id)
- explicit audiences/lists (union if multiple scopes define lists? wait)

Sophi: Clarification on audiences: for explicit allow-lists (e.g., `audience: [user123]`), we treat those as additive only if they exist at the same specificity? To avoid surprise, rule is: if the evaluator finds an explicit audience at a higher specificity, it uses that audience instead of falling back to lower audiences. We DO NOT union across scopes. Keep precedence consistent across types.

Kevin: TL;DR: precedence always by specificity; do not union numeric or list controls across scopes. For special safety we keep model-level disables absolute.

Taylor: PR opened for guardrail: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/412 (adds required-review metadata + e2e test). :tada:

Maria: Perfect, thanks all. If someone posts the doc link here I’ll sign off and then we can proceed with the encoder canary. :eyes:

deploy-bot: docbot created a stub: https://wiki.redwood.ai/eng-platform/flag-scope-precedence (stub added by @Samir)

Maria: Thanks — will review after lunch.
